attrs.evidence: lowering_check.mjs: lowering-is-deterministic (the same AST lowers to the same string twice, and the RELATION id is separate from the APPLICATION receipt), re-lowering-verifies (lowering again independently reaches the same target_term_sem_id, and add(3,2) reaches a different one so the id is not vacuous), out-of-fragment-refused (input, read, sub, a non-integer constant and a negative constant are each a NAMED refusal). native-execution-observed cross-checks the target term's identity against the C side: the kernel's target_term_sem_id equals ic32_canon's canonical id for the same lowered term, so both planes agree on what was fed in before either says what came out.
attrs.revision_note: SUPERSEDED at B1.2.1 and kept as history, superseded, not erased. Revision 1 described the PRE-B1.2 architecture in two places: it printed the LoweringReceipt as {program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}, the domain B1.2 moved onto the template, and it called the parameterized-versus-instantiated question DEFERRED three passes after B1 decided it and B1.1 ruled the framing a false choice. It also described lowering_sem_id as hashing 'the target term encoding id', which was true before the template existed and was the OVER-BINDING B1.2.1 removed. NO FALSE VERDICT WAS ACCEPTED: every witness the law cites ran and passed, and the mechanism was correct throughout -- what was stale was the record of what the mechanism does. Cited by ledger items 139 and earlier, which are history and stay as written.
attrs.statement: ONE SOURCE PROGRAM UNDER ONE LOWERING SEMANTICS DETERMINES ONE CANONICAL TARGET TERM. lowering_sem_id identifies the lowering SEMANTICS — H over the source core_sem_id, the target term encoding id, the canonical lowering specification and the conformance-vector identity — and is a different object from a record of what happened when a particular program was lowered, which is a LoweringReceipt {program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}. One id must not silently answer both 'which lowering semantics is this?' and 'what did lowering do here?'. THE INSTRUMENT IS RE-LOWERING, NOT A FILM. A semantic film is evidence for a TRANSITION SYSTEM; lowering is a relation DeriveProgram -> TargetTerm. Filming it would invent a sequence of internal compiler steps and make implementation strategy semantic — the mistake the read-order ruling refused when it kept access order out of the footprint. Verification is: re-lower the program independently under lowering_sem_id, canonicalise, and require target_term_sem_id to agree. DEFERRED AND NAMED: whether lowering is PARAMETERIZED (program -> target term with input ports, inputs arriving at execution, so target_term_sem_id is a function of the program alone) or INSTANTIATED (program + canonical_inputs -> closed target term, in which case the identity must say so). The first witness uses inputs={} and does not decide it. That decision comes BEFORE the input op, because an unstated variable inside target_term_sem_id is the hidden-identity bug class round 16 exists to prevent.
